idiom_name: gate traits mixed into a service (linearization orders them); Play Filter chain in web applications
implementation_notes: Scala composes gates as traits: a gate trait implements the guarded method by verifying and then delegating to an abstract inner service (a constructor parameter or a self-type), and a concrete service mixes the gates in, with trait linearization fixing the order so the outermost mixin checks first; each trait only names the one method it guards. What replaces the classic structure: trait mixins with abstract members replace the proxy class hierarchy, and Play's Filter / EssentialFilter chain - a curried nextFilter the filter either invokes or bypasses - replaces the hand-built chain in web applications. The classic proxy object is still justified when the guarded service is a final Java class or when gates must be added at runtime rather than by mixin at compile time.
pitfalls: Mixin linearization decides which gate checks first; mixing the traits in a different order silently changes the effective policy.
A gate trait that refers to an abstract inner service must have it initialised before the trait body runs, or the first request fails with a null instead of a compile error.
Play filters run after the router, and invoking an action directly from a filter bypasses the rest of the filter chain, which makes the remaining gates optional.
